messages:
incident-bot: ALERT — high p95/p99 latency and GPU mem pressure on continuous-batcher pool (us-west-2). affected service: runtime-prod, tag=continuous-batcher. autoscaler showing burst > 4x. severity: sev2 :fire:

alex: seeing the alert, grabbing on-call. paging tara and kevin now.

alex: quick check — are we seeing OOMs or just latency?

tara: p95 spiked ~2m ago, p99 > 12s. GPU mem util at 98% on several pods. some pods in CrashLoopBackOff.

kevin: getting `OOMKilled` events from kube, plus CUDA errors in the logs. pasting snippet:
```
2026-03-15T18:02:47Z runtime continuous-batcher[pid:3241] ERROR: cudaMemcpyAsync failed: out of memory
2026-03-15T18:03:01Z kernel: Killed process 3241 (batcher) total-vm:...
2026-03-15T18:03:05Z kubelet: Pod runtime-continuous-5d9f OOMKilled
```

alex: ok that's consistent w/ a runaway batch growth causing KV/cache to explode and push mem beyond quantization buffers.

jonah: quick context: we rolled a scheduler tweak earlier that increases dynamic batching window from 30ms -> 200ms for throughput wins. I think that change launched in the last deploy.

alex: @jonah can you confirm which deploy rolled that?

jonah: `deploy-bot` should have the deploy id.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-15_17:48:12 by jonah to runtime-prod continuous-batcher, config: dynamic_batch_window=200ms, max_batch_size=2048 -> active.

tara: that lines up. dynamic window blow-up + particular customer workload with long prompts created enormous batches and blocked the queue. queue length metric jumped from ~20 -> 480 in 90s.

kevin: logs show backlog queue size metric: `continuous_batch_queue_len: 472`. worker threads starving and some timeouts -> cascade.

alex: mitigation plan options — (1) rollback deploy to previous dynamic window 30ms, (2) set runtime override to cap batch size to 128, (3) kick over to dedicated-pool fallback for heavy traffic, (4) cordon nodes and drain bad pods. We need a fast temporary fix.

maria: product/customer-suc here — we have three paying customers on the affected route. one reported elevated latency to their telemetry. need ETA to notify them.

tara: immediate safe action: set `max_batch_size_override=128` via runtime feature flag; that is config-only, no restart, should gate growth. I can push that now.

kevin: +1 to config change first. rollback will take longer and is riskier during a surge.

jonah: doing the override now. patch command:
```bash
redwoodctl runtime set-config --pool continuous-batcher --set max_batch_size_override=128 --reason "hotfix batch growth"
```

jonah: applied. telemetry shows queue len dropping to ~60 in the last 30s.

alex: good. any pods still OOMing?

kevin: some pods remain in CrashLoop — OOMKilled persists for pods that hit OOM before the flag. kube is restarting them; new ones should be fine.

tara: I'm throttling the request routing for that route to reduce pressure while the system stabilizes. set route throttle to 0.5 qps per token.

maria: notifying impacted customers — ETA for stable back to normal?

alex: estimate 10-15m for queue to clear and for healthy pods to cycle. tell them we're mitigating and will follow up asap.

maria: sending message to the three customers now. quick note: "We've applied a temporary batch cap to mitigate an internal scheduling change that increased batch windows. You may see reduced throughput for a short time while we stabilize. We'll follow up with root cause."

jonah: follow-up check — scheduler rollback PR is prepared, but I want to run a small canary with the shorter window first.

tara: agree. canary the rollback to 1 node, monitor p99. if good, we do a full rollback.

kevin: we should also add an emergency circuit: auto-cap batches when GPU mem > 85% to prevent this class of issues. filing ticket.

alex: created post-incident task: INFRA-2142 "auto-cap batches on high GPU mem". assigning to eng-runtime squad.

deploy-bot: canary rollback deploy queued: deploy 2026-03-15_18:12:40 by jonah -> runtime-prod continuous-batcher (dynamic_batch_window=30ms).

jonah: canary started. monitoring.

tara: p99 back to ~1.2s on canary node, overall p99 trending down.

kevin: node flaps report: one G3 node hit hw error and flapped; cordoned and drained. creating node health ticket.

alex: tl;dr for incident channel: surge caused by new scheduler config (200ms) + long prompt workload -> batch growth -> GPU OOMs + pod crashes -> latency spike. mitigation: applied max_batch_size_override=128, throttled route, canary rollback to 30ms, cordoned flaky node. customer notif sent.

maria: thanks team. I'll coordinate postmortem comms with affected customers and include timeline.

tara: leaving followups: add automated mem-based cap, add deploy guard for dynamic window changes (flagged for gradual rollout only), improve alerting for sustained queue growth.

alex: closing on-call loop: if canary stays healthy for 20m, we'll roll to prod and mark incident resolved.

kevin: monitoring 10m snapshots, will update.

jonah: +1. updating the deploy PR with rollback notes.

incident-bot: UPDATE — incident severity lowered to sev3. next update scheduled in 10m. :white_check_mark:"
